topIssues.title: interop: Ensure new chains can be created post-interop
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Review the process for creating new chains post-interop and ensure it works with op-deployer/opcm and has suitable documentation. Need to decide on what is in scope for which releases - ie we could require new chains to continue to use pre-interop genesis then migrate and activate the fork initially but would need to document that (and at some point we will want to be able to create new chains with interop enabled at genesis).

Also need to decide whether/when to support deploying new chains into a dependency set together or if when deploying multiple chains in the same intent file they still go into their own separate dependency sets.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: SuperRoots for the unsafe
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
Currently, fetching super roots from supernode via atTimestamp fails if no verified or safe data exists at the referenced timestamp. It may be useful for supernode to return super roots in this case anyway.

I'm not fully convinced this is needed, but logging it here in case it proves useful later. It may make more sense to introduce a different RPC that provides possibly unverified super roots, so as to not complicate the atTimestamp RPC response.

topIssues.title: Add fast kona prestate build
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Problem
Acceptance testing depends on a Kona prestate, currently generated via just build-reproducible-prestates in the kona directory. This build uses Docker and is slower than necessary, which hurts local development velocity.

## Proposed Solution
Introduce a Docker-free Kona prestate build and wire it up to the cannon-prestates Makefile target. This will allow us to deprecate the cannon-kona-prestate CI job, since cannon-prestate-quick will handle Kona prestates as well.

topIssues.title: op-dispute-mon: ability to query supernode's VNs to get output roots
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The transition period for operators that run supernodes and op-dispute-mon will require running two instances of op-dispute-mon until the output root games have finalized. Currently, dispute-mon relies specifically on cl nodes to enrich FaultDisputeGames. And supernodes only to enrich SuperFaultDisputeGames. 

To simplify dispute-mon configuration and the infra around it, it would make sense for dispute-mon to query supernode's VNs to get output roots. This way one can run a dispute-mon that specifies only supernode-rpcs to monitor super and non-super dispute games.

topPRs.title: refactor(op-service/sources): minimal-fetch path for L2BlockRef and SystemConfig
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`L2Client.L2BlockRefBy{Label,Number,Hash}` and `SystemConfigByL2Hash` previously fetched the entire L2 block (`eth_getBlockByX` with `fullTx=true`) just to read a handful of header fields and decode the first transaction (the L1 info deposit). For large blocks this can waste >99% of the bandwidth and CPU. These methods sit on hot paths: engine FCU validation, attributes builder, sync startup.

This PR introduces a minimal-fetch path that downloads only the header (`fullTx=false`) plus the first transaction in a single batched JSON-RPC round trip. By-hash is naturally consistent. By-label / by-number do an optimistic consistency check (`header.Transactions[0] == tx.Hash()`) and refetch only the tx by the resolved hash on mismatch (rare race under reorg / new head).

## Stacking

This PR is stacked on **#20531** (`refactor(op-service/eth): remove BlockInfo Header() and HeaderRLP() escape hatches`). The base branch is set to `seb/refactor/blockinfo-cleanup` to keep the diff small. After #20531 merges, this PR retargets to `develop`.

## What changes

- **`eth.PayloadToInfo`** — new wrapper making `*ExecutionPayload` satisfy `BlockInfo` (now possible because the precursor PR removed `Header()` / `HeaderRLP()` from the interface).
- **`derive.BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit`** and **`derive.SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit`** — new inner helpers operating on `(BlockInfo, *types.Transaction)`. The existing `PayloadToBlockRef` and `PayloadToSystemConfig` become thin wrappers; behavior is preserved.
- **`EthClient.HeaderAndFirstTx`** — batched JSON-RPC call (`eth_getBlockByX(id, false)` + `eth_getTransactionByBlockXAndIndex(id, 0)`). Optimistic consistency check on label/number paths; tx-only refetch on mismatch using the resolved block hash. Skipped for by-hash paths.
- **`RPCHeaderWithTxHashes`** — new type to decode the `fullTx=false` response with transaction hashes (rather than full transactions).
- **`headerAndDepositCache`** — new LRU cache keyed by block hash, populated by `HeaderAndFirstTx`. Both `L2BlockRefByHash` and `SystemConfigByL2Hash` benefit from the same cache entry, since the engine FCU and attributes builder routinely call both for the same hash.
- **`L2Client` adapters rewritten** — `L2BlockRefBy{Label,Number,Hash}` and `SystemConfigByL2Hash` now go through `HeaderAndFirstTx` + the new derive helpers. Existing per-result caches (`l2BlockRefsCache`, `systemConfigsCache`) are preserved as the hot-path lookups.

## Behavior preserved

- Output of `L2BlockRefByX` and `SystemConfigByL2Hash` is identical to the previous full-payload path (verified by existing derivation, attributes-queue, and engine tests, all of which pass unchanged).
- Genesis short-circuit still handled (in the inner helpers).
- Deposit-type assertion still enforced.
- Existing `PayloadToBlockRef` and `PayloadToSystemConfig` callers (~25 sites across derivation, span batches, attributes) keep working — they call the new inner helpers via the preserved wrappers.

## Open items deferred

- Metrics for the consistency-check retry path. Add only if production data shows it firing measurably.
- Multi-block batching during sync (the `MultiCaller` pattern could batch K of these into one round trip). Out of scope here; a future optimization.
- The same minimal-fetch optimization applied to `EthClient.BlockRefBy{Label,Number,Hash}` (L1 side — header-only, no first-tx dependency). Independently valuable.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise exec -- go build ./...` passes
- [x] `mise exec -- just lint-go` passes (0 issues, mod tidy clean)
- [x] `mise exec -- go test -count=1 -short ./op-service/... ./op-program/... ./op-supernode/... ./op-interop-filter/... ./op-node/...` passes
- [x] `op-node/rollup/derive` test suite passes (covers the existing `PayloadToBlockRef` and `PayloadToSystemConfig` paths through their new thin-wrapper form)
- [ ] _Pending follow-up:_ dedicated unit tests for `HeaderAndFirstTx` (happy path, by-hash skip-check, label-race retry, deposit-type rejection) and for `BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit` / `SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit` parity vs. `PayloadTo*`. Existing test coverage transitively exercises the path through `L2BlockRefBy*`.

topPRs.title: docs: runbook for merging two chains into a shared dispute game
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds a chain-operator runbook for merging two pre-interop OP Stack chains onto a shared `DisputeGameFactory`, `AnchorStateRegistry`, and `ETHLockbox` via `OPContractsManagerMigrator.migrate`.

- Uses `op-fetcher` (with `--output-file`) for L1 address/role lookups in pre- and post-migration states; keeps direct `cast`/`curl` checks for the feature-flag, CGT, respected-game-type, supernode-sync, and prestate-server preconditions.
- Distinguishes the privileged `proposer`/`challenger` roles on `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` from the wallet `op-challenger` actually signs with.
- Calls out an explicit step to start the shared `op-challenger` and `op-dispute-mon` as soon as the shared factory is verified, since `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` is permissionless and games can be created — and resolved — by anyone the moment the factory is live.

Companion to the existing single-chain "Upgrading a Chain From Output Roots to Super Roots" runbook.

topPRs.title: feat(op-acceptance): after-chain-head tests via TestSequencer (alt to #20349)
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Alternative implementation of ethereum-optimism/optimism#20349.

#20349 ports 6 *AfterChainHead* subtests but also rewrites the existing `RunSuperFaultProofTest` / `RunVariedBlockTimesTest` Stage 1 and Stage 2 setup, and its Stage 2b's `StartSequencer → Reached → StopSequencer` dance has an unbounded race under CI scheduling pauses (a pause of any length between two of those calls produces unbounded sequencer overshoot, which `LocalSafe` then catches up to once batchers re-submit).

This PR keeps Stage 1 / Stage 2 **byte-identical to develop** (zero deletions vs develop) and replaces Stage 2b with deterministic block production via `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlock` (already exposed through `SimpleInterop`):

- Stops batchers + sequencers, waits for both safety levels to stall.
- `SequenceBlock(parent = current head)` once per chain — produces exactly one block at `parent.Time + blockTime`, no wall-clock dependence, no `Reached/Stop` race.
- Iterative-convergence catch-up: extends whichever chain is below the current max, re-derives max each iteration, terminates only when *all* chain heads are equal (handles 1 s + 2 s mixed configurations and arbitrary pre-Stage-2b chain drift).
- Restarts batchers briefly to land boundary blocks on L1, validates via supernode, captures `l1HeadAdvanced`, stops batchers.
- `claimTimestamp = boundaryTimestamp + 5` — derived from settled state.

Tests 5/6 reference `boundary+2` and `boundary+3` (boundary-relative trace indices). Sequencers stay stopped after Stage 2b so no chain has blocks past `boundary`; batchers stop after submitting boundary so no L1 batch covers anything past it. The supernode returns `InvalidTransition` at those indices deterministically.

Single-file change: `op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go`, +344 / −0 vs develop.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs ×5` on initial implementation (44/44 subtests per run, 135–169 s each)
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs ×1` on the convergence fix (44/44 subtests, 180 s)
- [ ] `TestPreinteropFaultProofs ×5` (not yet executed locally)
- [ ] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes` and `_FasterChainB` ×5 each (still `MarkFlaky` for ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828 — confirm this PR doesn't make that worse)
